question: Which statement best describes Constraining with extends?
options: Constrain T to an interface/object type so the body can use that shape's members. `<T extends { id: number }>` means every T has an id, so the function can read item.id safely while still accepting any object that has an id (plus more).

The classic constraint for safe property access: T is the object type and K is restricted to T's actual keys (keyof T). This guarantees `obj[key]` is valid and lets the return type be the exact value type T[K], not any. Passing a key that doesn't exist becomes a compile error.

A type parameter can have a default used when none is supplied or inferred: `<T = string>`. Defaults and constraints combine: `<T extends object = {}>` constrains T to objects and defaults it to {}. The default must itself satisfy the constraint.
